context.description: Harness tool calls reach the supervisor that owns the session

evidence.trustReason: Given a builder session claimed by its task supervisor: a real harness root spawns the real run supervisor as run:<runID>; the real T1.3 task supervisor claims its session through TaskHarness.claimSession, and ownerOf(session) is asserted to equal {owner: task:<run>:T1.3, watch: true} (watch false for the verifier session). When task_ready / verdict / a repeat past the limit: the scripted model calls the REAL tools from SessionPrompt.createTaskHarnessTools with harness.hooks and the REAL TaskHooks.repetitionStop that prompt.ts calls. Then the owner receives the event and records its fact when the turn ends: each test asserts the supervisor context holds the event (ready true; the exact verdicts; repeated = 'repetition: 3 identical bash calls in a row', limit 3 read from the owner, none for 1 and 2 calls), that no task.ready / task.verified / task.repeated is stored while the held turn runs, and that the fact is stored after the release with at >= release time (task.ready head holds the builder's file; task.verified carries the sent verdicts). And an unowned session records nothing and the tool says so: task_ready and verdict answer 'No task harness run owns this session. Nothing was recorded.' with valid false, limitOf and repetitionStop are none, the stored facts and the owner's context do not change. And every claim of a run is removed when the run ends: a real TaskCommand.job ends by its run wall clock (run.ended failed) and, in a second job, by a cancel (run.cancelled); in both the builder and S2 judge claims are gone, another run's claim stays, the run is not running, and a later task_ready in the ended session says so and records nothing. Fresh run: 5 pass, 0 fail, 51 expect calls.
